design.heading: Core entities
paragraphs: The core of the protocol: a root Identity derived from a seed phrase, contextual Handles, and stateless signed sessions.

Nothing here is stored or looked up: a server verifies a session with one signature check, and a third party verifies delegated access using only your root public key. Attestation chains carry audiences, scopes and TTL caps enforced at verification time — trust can be delegated, and revoked, without sharing a private key.

included.text: from a 64-byte seed or a 12/24-word BIP39 phrase — constant forever, stored nowhere.
a separate Ed25519 keypair per context; compromising one reveals nothing about the others.
parent-signed grants with audiences, scopes and TTL caps, verified offline by any third party.
verifyStateless for your backend, verifyAttested for partners — with instant branch revocation.
deterministic passwords, channel keys and X25519 shared secrets, plus BIP39 passphrase support.

development.heading: End-to-end encryption
paragraphs: Protocol cryptography for real communication: canonical Signal X3DH, long-lived encrypted channels, and envelopes for recipients who are offline.

Channels derive a fresh key for every message and rotate epochs, so what was encrypted stays sealed even if a key leaks later. Pre-keys make asynchronous delivery work: you can encrypt for someone who hasn't been online for days. Underneath sit audited primitives — HKDF, X25519, AES-256-GCM — with Argon2id protecting passwords at the edges.

included.text: Signal's key agreement with mandatory one-time pre-keys — no zero-fallback, MITM-resistant.
per-message keys, strictly-increasing replay protection, epoch rotation at defined points.
X3DH-wrapped keys reach recipients who haven't been online; every envelope is self-contained.
named profiles for interactive and sensitive use, strength checks and HIBP breach lookup.
HKDF against RFC 5869 test vectors, X25519, AES-256-GCM, secure key wipe.

performance.heading: React SDK
paragraphs: React bindings that turn the protocol into product UI: identity hooks, seed-phrase screens, self-renewing sessions.

The seed phrase is the one secret users must never lose — so its UX is part of the security model. Words are shown once, verified by an order grid, validated word by word on import. Derived keys persist only as non-extractable CryptoKeys, isolated per identity. A headless layer keeps every state machine framework-agnostic — the future @me2em/sdk.

included.text: useCreateIdentity, useImportSeed, useHandle, useSubHandle — the full identity lifecycle.
show-once display, single copy, order-verification grid, per-word import validation.
useSession tracks expiry and auto-renews at half-life.
per-identity IndexedDB isolation with non-extractable persisted CryptoKeys.
framework-agnostic state machines with zero React imports.

payments.heading: x402 v2 payment transport
paragraphs: The wire layer of machine-to-machine payments: a base64 header codec pinned to the upstream x402 v2 golden vectors, and a payment-aware fetch client that turns a 402 into one signed retry.

Transport, not policy: who pays is decided by attestation, how much by the PaymentRequest, how it executes by a chain adapter, and who confirms by the facilitator. The Me2eM extra.me2em extension rides the same wire — identity metadata on every payment artifact.

included.text: PAYMENT-REQUIRED / PAYMENT-SIGNATURE / PAYMENT-RESPONSE — base64, golden-vector pinned.
createPaymentFetch: 402 → sign exactly once → replay. Never pays twice.
paymentRequiredResponse, readPaymentHeader, settlementHeader — the 402 handshake in three calls.
withMe2emExtra / readMe2emExtra — Me2eM identity metadata on the x402 wire.
FacilitatorClient interface plus an opt-in B402 facilitator (@experimental).

chain.heading: Solana chain adapter
paragraphs: The first chain in the payment stack: deterministic wallet trees derived from the same 64-byte seed as your Identity, so one seed phrase carries both who you are and where your SOL lives.

Verification is fail-closed and chain-side: a settlement is checked in the normative order — not found, wrong reference, expired, replayed, wrong recipient, underpaid. The x402 signer is offline by construction: the blockhash is injected, never fetched.

included.text: SolanaWalletTree.fromSeed — m/44'/501'/{i}'/0' SLIP-0010 over the Identity seed; nextPaymentIndex allocation.
SolanaWalletAdapter + SolanaPaymentAdapter per exact chain; registerSolanaAdapters in one call.
verifyPayment in the normative failure order; on-curve verifyWalletBinding.
SOL-only pay, seed per call, reference rides the transaction.
SolanaX402Signer — legacy-transfer signing with blockhash by injection.

process.heading: From seed to verified session — and settled payment
process.lead: Five steps — the same in every scenario, from a messenger to a charging network to a paid API.

steps.title: Write the seed
steps.description: 12 or 24 BIP39 words on paper. The only permanent carrier of identity — never transmitted, never stored.

steps.title: Derive the root
steps.description: The Identity is computed locally by HKDF. Handles for each context — work, personal, devices — derive offline from it.

steps.title: Delegate & sign
steps.description: Attestation chains grant scoped, time-boxed access to devices, partners, and AI agents. Sessions are stateless signed tokens.

steps.title: Verify & revoke
steps.description: Any third party verifies with the root public key alone. One revoked jti disables an entire branch — instantly.

steps.title: Pay & settle
steps.description: The same seed derives a deterministic Solana wallet. A 402 response carries the PaymentRequest; the client signs once, replays, and the facilitator settles on-chain. The buyer verifies with the seller's public root — no ledger.

glossary.heading: Speak the protocol
glossary.lead: A shared vocabulary for the whole model — each term is defined once, here, and used everywhere else.

terms.definition: Root cryptographic identity derived from a seed phrase. Constant forever.
A derived, attested, named key representing a distinct identity context.
A leaf child of a Handle.
A parent-signed statement binding a child key to a name and a grant.
A long-lived E2EE relationship derived from an X3DH shared secret.
Key bytes existing only in RAM at the moment of use.
TTL-bound rotating material (SPK/OTK, cache keys, session tokens).
A chain-agnostic payment contract: amount, recipient wallet, reference, expiry. Transported over x402 v2.
One implementation per exact CAIP-2 chain: pay and verifyPayment against the chain.
The on-curve link between a Handle and its derived wallet — verified without a ledger.
The on-chain execution of a PaymentRequest, confirmed by the facilitator and verifiable by either party.
The service that verifies a signed payment and settles it on-chain — the x402 v2 counterparty.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: The questions that come up before the first derivation.

items.question: Do I need to register anywhere?
items.answer: No. An Identity is derived from your seed phrase on your device. There is no account to create — and no database that could leak it.

items.question: What happens if I lose my seed phrase?
items.answer: The identity is unrecoverable — by design. The seed is the only permanent carrier of identity; there is no reset link because there is nothing on a server to reset.

items.question: Is Me2eM a blockchain?
items.answer: No. Derivation and verification are pure cryptography — Ed25519 and HKDF — offline, with no network and no consensus. A session verifies in about a millisecond.

items.question: Is it production-ready?
items.answer: The packages are release candidates — core 1.0.0-rc.7, crypto 1.1.0-rc.2, react 1.0.0-rc.4, x402 1.0.0-rc.1, solana 1.1.0-rc.1 — moving toward a v1.0 API freeze. Fine for evaluation and prototypes today; pin versions and expect changes in production.

items.question: Which verification mode should I use?
items.answer: verifyStateless for backends you control — they already hold the root key. verifyAttested for anyone else: grants are enforced at verification time, with the root public key only.

items.question: How deep can the hierarchy go?
items.answer: Identity → Handle → SubHandle, where SubHandle is the leaf (MAX_DEPTH = 2). A device derives its own SubHandles and child attestations — fully offline.

items.question: Can I revoke a device or an AI agent?
items.answer: Yes. Revoking one attestation jti disables the entire branch — current and future sessions — on every verifier that checks revocations.

items.question: Where do I report a vulnerability?
items.answer: See SECURITY.md in the me2em-protocol repository — responsible disclosure, with credit.

items.question: Is it free to use?
items.answer: Yes, completely free. The Me2eM protocol is Apache-2.0 licensed (with patent grant). The theme is MIT licensed — use it for personal and commercial projects, no attribution required.

items.question: Who maintains Me2eM?
items.answer: Me2eM is developed on a voluntary basis: the protocol, the packages, and this website are maintained by volunteers under the me2em-org organization on GitHub. The project needs sponsorship — contributions directly fund development and infrastructure.

items.question: Why is the protocol name capitalised the way it is?
items.answer: "Me2eM" is the only correct form in human-facing prose. The all-lowercase variant is reserved for machine identifiers (code, URLs, packages). The brand does not decline or conjugate — the "iPhone rule". The full rules live in the Brand Guidelines.

items.question: Can I use the Me2eM code, name, and logo?
items.answer: Yes. The protocol source (GitHub) is licensed under Apache 2.0, and this website under MIT. The name and logo may be used to refer to the protocol and compatible implementations, provided the brand canon is respected: the name is written Me2eM, the logo is used as-is. Full rules: Brand Guidelines.

items.question: Where is the documentation?
items.answer: All documentation lives at /docs — core guides, API references, glossary, and quick starts. Package references: @me2em/core, @me2em/crypto, @me2em/react.

items.question: How do I report a vulnerability?
items.answer: Email security@me2em.com — this is the only private channel. See SECURITY.md in the protocol repository for details.

items.question: How can I contribute?
items.answer: Check CONTRIBUTING.md in the protocol repository for guidelines on filing issues, opening pull requests, and joining discussions.

meta.title: Seed-Derived Identity Protocol
meta.description: One seed phrase, many isolated Handles, stateless sessions and delegatable trust. A decentralized identity protocol on Ed25519.

hero.titleLine3: One Identity → Many Handles → Stateless Sessions
hero.description: A decentralized, seed-derived identity, authorization and payment protocol built on Ed25519 — one seed phrase grows into many isolated identities for people, IoT fleets and AI agents.
hero.descriptionMobile: A decentralized, seed-derived identity protocol on Ed25519 — for people, IoT fleets and AI agents.

intro.heading: The whole idea in one paragraph
intro.body: Me2eM grows one seed phrase into as many separate identities as you need: one for every app, device and AI agent, each derived on your own device. Access is delegated and revoked with a signature, and signing in takes the server a single signature check. The same seed derives a Solana wallet, so any identity can pay for what it uses — API calls settle on-chain. One user, safely many: separate profiles for work and home, fleets of devices and drones, and AI agents that act only within the permissions you signed for them.

packages.heading: Five packages, one seed
packages.lead: Everything derives from the same Ed25519 root — start with the core, add encryption, UI, and payments when you need them.

cards.title: @me2em/core
cards.description: Core primitives for the Me2eM authorization protocol: hierarchical deterministic identities, stateless signed sessions, and parent-signed attestation for delegatable, externally verifiable authorization.

cards.title: @me2em/crypto
cards.description: Cryptographic mechanisms for the Me2eM protocol: E2EE channels, X3DH key exchange, purpose-based key derivation, and envelope patterns for offline recipients and media chunk encryption.

cards.title: @me2em/react
cards.description: React bindings for the Me2eM protocol: identity lifecycle hooks, seed-phrase UX components, session management, and an encrypted per-identity context cache.

cards.title: @me2em/x402
cards.description: x402 v2 payment transport: the base64 header codec, a payment-aware fetch client (402 → sign once → replay, never pays twice), server helpers, and the Me2eM extra.me2em extension. Transport, not policy — who pays is decided by attestation, how it settles by an adapter.

cards.title: @me2em/solana
cards.description: Solana chain adapter: deterministic wallet trees over SLIP-0010 (m/44'/501'/{i}'/0') derived from the same 64-byte seed as your Identity, on-chain payment verification in the normative failure order, programmatic pay, and the offline x402 PaymentSigner.

workWithMe.heading: Guaranteed by cryptography
workWithMe.lead: Nine properties of the protocol — math, not promises.

cards.title: Seed-derived
cards.description: Your identity lives in a seed phrase; keys are recomputed on demand. A breached server holds nothing.

cards.title: Zero-knowledge
cards.description: Private keys never leave your device. Servers verify signatures without ever learning who you are.

cards.title: Deterministic
cards.description: Same seed, same keys — always. One identity on every device, with nothing to sync.

cards.title: Isolated
cards.description: Every Handle is a separate keypair. Compromising one context reveals nothing about the others.

cards.title: Stateless
cards.description: No session database. Any server — or any third party — verifies a token with one signature check.

cards.title: Delegatable
cards.description: Attestation chains hand scoped, time-boxed access to partners, IoT devices, and AI agents.

cards.title: Hierarchical
cards.description: Identity → Handle → SubHandle: a whole device fleet under one root, provisioned offline.

cards.title: Revocable
cards.description: One revoked attestation disables an entire branch — current and future sessions, instantly.

cards.title: Chain-agnostic payments
cards.description: A Handle is a buyer, an attested entity is a seller. x402 v2 carries signed payment artifacts over plain HTTP; Solana ships first, adapters plug in per chain.

stack.heading: The stack
stack.lead: Audited primitives and a lean toolchain — every tile links to its source.
